persona: Cheerful but annoyed with herself. Had new wheels and tyres fitted on the morning of the accident; has the wheel receipt, the quote and a photo on her phone.
initial_message: Hi, I need to make a claim for my car. On Saturday 5 September at about 4pm I hit a high kerb pulling into a park at the Rototuna shops. The front left wheel is gouged and bent on the rim and the bumper corner is cracked. I had only had new wheels fitted that morning! No one was hurt and the car is still drivable.

facts.incident.description: I was pulling forward into an angle park outside the shops and misjudged the high concrete kerb. The front left wheel hit it hard and the bumper corner scraped along it.
facts.incident.location: Shops car park on Bellbird Test Drive, Rototuna, Hamilton
facts.incident.cause: Misjudged the distance to a high concrete kerb while parking
facts.loss.description: Front left alloy wheel gouged and bent on the outer rim; lower left corner of the front bumper cracked
facts.policyholder.name: Mere Ridgefern
facts.vehicle.damage_description: Outer rim of the front left alloy wheel deeply gouged with a bent section about 10 cm long; a crack about 12 cm long in the lower left corner of the front bumper. The tyre still holds air.
facts.driver.name: Mere Ridgefern
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the wheel and the bumper corner, taken at the shops. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Totara Brook Body Works dated 14 September 2026, total $1,541.00 including GST. Available now.
facts.wheels.description: Four Stratos 19-inch gloss black alloy wheels with Kinetra tyres
facts.wheels.purchase_price: $3,480.00 for the four wheels and tyres
facts.evidence.receipt: Receipt from Awa Field Automotive for the wheels and tyres, dated 5 September 2026. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_date: Yes, the wheels and tyres were fitted that morning, on 5 September, and I hit the kerb the same afternoon. Very annoying.
facts.if_asked_how_far_driven_after: I drove home slowly, about 3 km. The steering felt normal.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo taken from slightly above, close-up of the front left wheel of a white compact SUV parked beside a high concrete kerb. The gloss black alloy wheel is shiny and new, with a plain gloss black centre cap, but its outer rim lip is deeply gouged with bright silver scrapes and a visibly bent section near the kerb. Above it the lower corner of the white front bumper has a short crack and grey scuff marks. The tyre sidewall is smooth plain black rubber. Afternoon daylight, dry asphalt. The frame shows only the wheel, the tyre, the wheel arch and the bumper corner. No text, no logos, no people.

design.notes: Innocent control: the wheels were bought and fitted on 5 September 2026 and damaged the same afternoon. Bought and lost on the same New Zealand calendar day is not after the loss; at least one day is needed (rules, section 3).

triage.rationale: Single vehicle against a kerb, nobody hurt, car drivable, a photo, a complete quote at NZD 1,541.00 including GST and a receipt for the wheels, policy on file. The receipt date is the incident day itself, which is not after the loss. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Purchase date 5 September 2026 is the incident day, not after it; the check needs at least one day after the last possible incident day

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 February 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2021-02-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
